item.title: Middle East live: Iran should not use Hormuz to ‘blackmail’ Gulf, Qatar says
item.description: Qatar’s top diplomat said on Tuesday that Iran should not use the Strait of Hormuz as a means to blackmail Gulf countries or as a “weapon”. Iran’s ongoing blockade of the strait has halted crucial oil and gas exports for many Gulf countries, straining their economies. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Iranians mourn children killed in US bombing of school
item.description: It remains the deadliest single attack in the war on Iran so far. On the 28th February, a missile strike hit a school in Minab in Hormozgan Province. 155 people died, including 120 children. According to US media, a preliminary American military investigation found that the strike was made in error: the actual target was an adjacent Islamic Revolutionary Guards Military Base. FRANCE 24's correspondent Ali al-Basha gained rare access to the bombsite, he brings us this report.

item.title: Iranians concerned about war extending as Iran and US fail to find common ground
item.description: As Donald Trump rejects Iran's counterproposals, Tehran has reacted saying that the Iranian government doesn't care if the United States aren't happy with the proposals. The United States had agreed to lifting such sanctions and freeing funds, but it first wants Iran to halt uranium enrichment and hand over its stocks. Residents in the capital are concerned about the war extending despite the current ceasefire.

item.title: Trump says Iran ceasefire on 'life support' after rejecting Tehran counteroffer
item.description: US President Donald Trump warned Monday that the fragile ceasefire in the Middle East war was on "life support" after rejecting Iran’s latest counterproposal, as Tehran vowed its military was ready to respond to any aggression and fears of a prolonged energy crisis sent oil prices surging.

item.title: Iran warns of retaliation as US tensions threaten fragile peace talks
item.description: Tensions between the United States and Iran have escalated after reports of US fire on Iranian-linked tankers in the Gulf of Oman. Tehran warned of retaliation against American targets in the region as diplomatic efforts continue over a proposed deal involving sanctions, nuclear limits, and maritime security.

item.title: Trump shuts down Iran's response to US peace proposal
item.description: Iran, which on Sunday sent its response to the latest US ceasefire proposal, wants negotiations to focus on permanently ending the war. However, US President Donald Trump quickly rejected it as “totally unacceptable”. He did not explain why. Iran seeks to end the war on all fronts, including in Lebanon, where Israel is fighting the Iranian-backed Hezbollah militant group, and to ensure the security of shipping. Follow our blog to see how the day's events unfolded.

item.title: Israel strikes kill several in Lebanon despite truce
item.description: Israel carried out strikes across Lebanon on Saturday, killing at least nine people in the south according to authorities, with raids also targeting a highway not far from Beirut outside of Hezbollah's traditional strongholds. The fresh attacks were some of the most intense since the start of a three-week-old ceasefire between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah that has done little to halt daily exchanges of fire, mostly in southern Lebanon.

item.title: Iran keeps US waiting for response on ceasefire plan
item.description: Iran on Saturday questioned the seriousness of US diplomacy while keeping Washington waiting for a response to its latest negotiating position in the wake of renewed naval clashes in the Gulf. A parallel ceasefire on the war's Lebanon front is also under strain amid daily exchanges of fire between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah.

item.title: Independent Israeli report accuses Hamas of 'systematic' sexual violence during October 7 attacks
item.description: A new independent commission finds Hamas and its allies committed "systematic, widespread" sexual violence during their October 7, 2023 attack on Israel and against hostages they took back to Gaza. This comes as the Knesset passed a law establishing a special military tribunal to try Palestinian militants accused of taking part in the October 7 attacks, under which the death penalty could be handed down. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky tells us more form Jerusalem.

item.title: Israel launches strikes on south Lebanon after warning residents to evacuate
item.description: The Israeli military launched strikes across southern Lebanon on Saturday after issuing evacuation warnings for several villages in the area, saying it was targeting Hezbollah positions despite an existing ceasefire.
